scores.evidence: Input sanitization stops ~80% of naive injection; token cap + fail-closed + opaque prompts stop the rest.
scores.rationale: Confidence is defined as average similarity score and used as the answer-quality gate, the injection defense is overstated, and the 'hallucination mitigation' row says 'changing strategy requires retraining'. There is also a 'gpt-4o-turbo-mini' model and 'Forbid I don't know'.

scores.evidence: Support agent or internal user submits a query... No customer access until Phase 2.
scores.rationale: It gives a buildable phased RAG with escalation, but it mostly targets internal agents, handles deletion and visibility weakly, and treats the customer-facing need as an afterthought.

scores.evidence: Forbid "I don't know" — redirect to human support.
scores.rationale: That contradicts the later prompt line 'If the help-center does not cover the topic, say so'. Help-center docs are called internal and non-PII, yet customers get access. Phase labels for customer exposure also conflict (Phase 2 vs Phase 3 vs Phase 4).

scores.evidence: Create 300 held-out queries... Acceptance: <5% hallucination, >95% source accuracy.
scores.rationale: Early gates (V0–V3) are tied to the risks with checkable thresholds and a canary. However, thresholds are invented, there is no regression eval rerun on every change (only Phase 5 mentions it), and sample sizes are small.

scores.evidence: Missing inputs (pull forward early): Help-center doc volume and format... Customer data in help-center docs
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labelled and missing inputs are listed, but some figures are presented as fact (p50 ~1s, cost ~$0.008, 80% injection stop rate), and the 'docs are internal' claim is asserted.

scores.evidence: Circuit breaker: if LLM API fails >5% of the time in a 5-min window, fall back to manual support
scores.rationale: Covers LLM outages, timeouts, retries, idempotent ingestion and injection tests. It misses stale or deleted content handling, retrieval-time access control, and indirect injection from content, and its injection handling is weak.

scores.evidence: Feature flag `enable_support_chatbot: false` (default off)... Pod drain, old image revert
scores.rationale: Covers canary, rollback, alerts, on-call, runbooks and cost alerts. It is somewhat heavy for the team (Kubernetes, Helm, multi-region, chaos engineering) and ownership is partly vague.

scores.evidence: Starting assumption: 2–10 USD/1M tokens; 500–2k tokens per query. Accept <$0.01 cost per answer.
scores.rationale: It identifies inference as the main driver, with token caps, budget gates, alerts and a model-swap path. Some of the numbers are inconsistent (<$0.01 vs <$0.02) and unsupported, and caching and rate limiting are thin.

scores.evidence: Reversibility | R3 ... Configurable model endpoint (allow swap to Claude, Llama, etc.)
scores.rationale: Decisions carry reversibility tags, a spike to choose the backend, and an abstraction for the model. The R1/R2/R3 labels are inconsistent, and the schema and metadata model are not treated as one-way.

scores.evidence: Multi-region failover (optional... Chaos engineering... Prometheus or CloudWatch; Kubernetes pod... Helm chart
scores.rationale: The core pipeline is simple and linear, and the plan defers multi-turn, self-hosting and other extras. There is boilerplate in the cross-cutting sections and the AI-layer table, and the five-phase cadence is heavy, while essentials like access control and deletion are under-built.

scores.evidence: Chunk docs (500 token window, 50 token overlap)... Run 100 end-to-end queries... Acceptance: p99 latency <5s
scores.rationale: The build order is concrete and gated with checkable results and failure fallbacks. There are leftover inconsistencies and some leaked template text, such as 'Principle 7' and 'The plan method'.

checklist.evidence: Each update triggers re-ingestion (automated job, weekly or on-demand).
Chunk docs (500 token window, 50 token overlap)... Add metadata: {doc_id, title, source_url, chunk_index}.
Create 300 held-out queries (not used in retrieval tuning) from help-center docs.
If the help-center does not cover the topic, say so and suggest contacting support.
Route escalation to support queue (Zendesk, Slack, etc.). Log reason: "low confidence", "out of scope", "LLM error".
Hard token cap... input sanitization... No tool call or code execution.
Redaction / masking of PII/secrets in help-center docs before ingestion
Build regex/pattern list (e.g., "billing" → not in help-center docs; escalate immediately).
Weekly: analyze thumbs-down responses; identify patterns (e.g., "docs are outdated"
Hard token cap (1500 output tokens)... alert if p95 latency >5s or daily cost >$50

traps.evidence: Cite source always + human review flag for low-confidence answers
Confirm: help-center docs contain no customer PII, no credentials, no sensitive product details that should not be in public chat.
RAG + hosted API: no fine-tune, easier to iterate
Model evaluation suite (benchmark new models vs. incumbent on standard test set before promotion)
Simple linear: sanitize → embed → retrieve → prompt → LLM → response → log.

note: The plan is a well-gated phased RAG rollout with real validation gates, cost and ops controls, but it is weak on document visibility, deletion handling, structure-aware chunking, PII and provider terms, and regression evals. It also contradicts itself on declining to answer.
